headline: Growth accelerates, guidance raised on AI-driven demand
summary_short: Flex reported Q1 FY2027 net sales of $7,928M, up 20.6% y/y and 6.0% q/q, with GAAP EPS of $0.76 (+52% y/y) and record adjusted EPS of $1.00; GAAP operating margin was 4.9%, up from 4.7% a year ago.
summary_long: Net sales rose 20.6% y/y and 6.0% q/q to $7,928M, driven by strength in AI/data-center infrastructure and the recent Electrical Power Products acquisition. GAAP operating margin held at 4.9% (vs 4.7% y/y) as adjusted operating margin expanded to 6.7% from 6.0% y/y on higher volumes offsetting higher SG&A and acquisition-related legal/other costs (~$53M spin-off costs, $14M acquisition costs). GAAP EPS rose to $0.76 from $0.50 y/y; adjusted EPS reached a record $1.00. Free cash flow fell to $41M from $268M y/y as capex nearly doubled to $236M and working capital absorbed $149M. Cash rose to $2,840M and long-term debt rose to $5,219M. Flex raised full-year FY2027 guidance across net sales, margin, and EPS, and issued Q2 guidance.

drivers.explanation: CEO Advaithi attributed the quarter to continued execution of Flex's strategy, including joining the S&P 500 and expanding its role in AI infrastructure, which strengthened its position in growth markets.

The release does not break out revenue by segment or geography in this exhibit; management's only stated cause is the general strategic narrative above (AI-infrastructure demand, S&P 500 inclusion), not a revenue-specific driver.
Gross margin expanded to 9.4% from 8.7% y/y because cost of sales grew 19.9% y/y, slightly slower than revenue's 20.6% growth; the release does not discuss gross profit as a distinct line.

Revenue growth and modest gross-margin expansion were partly offset by higher SG&A (Electrical Power Products acquisition scaling) and ~$53M spin-off-related plus $14M acquisition-related legal/other costs disclosed in Schedule V.
EPS growth (+52% y/y) outpaced net income growth (+48% y/y, to $285M from $192M) because diluted share count fell 1.8% y/y to 374M from 381M.
Mirrors the diluted EPS move above; both reflect the same net income growth against a comparable basic-share count, per Schedule I.
Cash from operations fell to $276M from $399M y/y mainly on a $149M working-capital drag this quarter versus a $65M working-capital source a year ago, despite higher net income.
